title: Portfolio Optimization Methodology
acceptance_criteria: Audit the actual expected-return calculation: confirm which price field is used, whether returns are simple or log, the sampling frequency, the estimator, the annualization method, how missing data is handled, and how the common-history window across ETFs is determined.
Audit the covariance estimator: confirm estimator choice, frequency, annualization, alignment across assets, NaN handling, and any positive-semidefinite stabilization applied.
Expose the actual Maximum Sharpe optimization formula, the risk-free rate used, and every constraint applied to the optimizer.
Add post-optimization validation of constraints and reported metrics (weights sum to 1, bounds respected, reported risk/return/Sharpe consistent with the optimized weights).
Do not backward-fill data prior to an ETF's inception and do not silently drop ETFs with insufficient history; insufficient-history behavior must be explicit and surfaced to the user.
If present-day optimized weights are ever applied backward over historical dates, that output must be labeled 'Fixed-Allocation Historical Backtest', never 'walk-forward'.
Add compact methodology and runtime-settings UI/metadata describing the above, backed by deterministic automated tests.
prohibited: Do not silently replace the existing sample covariance estimator with Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage or any other estimator without explicit disclosure.
Do not add Black-Litterman, CAPM, true walk-forward optimization, Monte Carlo simulation, VaR, or sentiment-driven features as part of this task.
